messages:
alice: Quick sync 1: reproducible cold-starts on encrypted safetensors bundles. Small requests hit ~1.7s. Root cause looks like synchronous payload decrypt + eager mmap of many tiny shards. Thinking: manifest-first + decrypt-backoff/circuit for payloads

Tom: Decrypt-backoff? elaborate please.

alice: Idea: decrypt a signed manifest quickly (manifest small) and schedule a minimal ready set. For payloads, use a token-bucket + exponential backoff on KMS calls per-host to avoid bursts when many bundles arrive at once. Also expose a circuit-breaker on payload decrypts so we can fail fast to fallback model variants.

irene: Nice. That addresses KMS quota storms. How do we pick the minimal ready set?

alice: Manifest includes per-shard role tags: {role: kv|embed|base|quant_delta}. For tiny prefixes we warm kv first. Runtime provides a policy function get_minimum_roles(request_profile) -> ["kv"] or ["kv","base"]. Loader marks model ready when all shards for those roles are ready.

Tom: What about precision overlays (quant deltas)? Could we apply them lazily and still run?

alice: Yes. Expose two states: READY_BASE and READY_QUANT. Runtime can start inference at READY_BASE and receive event on_precision_applied when overlays are done. We track metrics to detect regressions after overlay.

irene: Circuit-breaker details? When tripping, do we abort and fall back to smaller model, or keep retrying in background?

alice: Configurable. Default policy: trip on 5 consecutive decrypt errors or if concurrent_payload_decrypts > host_limit. On trip: mark this bundle degraded and serve fallback variant if available, while background worker retries with backoff (initial 100ms, factor 2, max 5s). Also emit alerts.

Tom: How do we avoid trusting untrusted manifests that claim roles to push high-cost shards early?

alice: Manifests must be signed. Loader verifies signature against allowed registries. If signature absent or bad, treat roles as unknown and use conservative ordering (base then kv). Signed manifests include signer_key_version stored in manifest cache for TTL and invalidation hooks.

irene: For Dedicated vs Private: sidecar per-host or central?

alice: Default per-host sidecar for latency. Private customers can run a central decryptor inside their VPC. The design needs to note KMS call cost and recommend header caching + HSM/local KMS proxy for high QPS.

Tom: Observability we need: manifest_decrypt_ms, manifest_sig_verify_ms, payload_decrypt_attempts, decrypt_failures, circuit_trips, time_to_min_ready_ms, time_to_quant_ready_ms, kms_calls_per_min. Also expose current token-bucket depth in metrics.

alice: Ops safety: implement host-level semaphore for concurrent payload decrypts, tenant-level token-bucket for warmups, and a scheduling cost model that assigns a warmup_cost per shard so a manifest can't immediately drain resources.

irene: Fallbacks for missing shards? Try replica -> re-download bundle -> fallback model variant. Also a repair queue that tries to re-fetch problematic shards offline and marks status when fixed.

platform-bot: Created INF-6121: "manifest-first + decrypt-backoff + circuit-breaker" (owner: alice, reviewers: tom, irene).

Tom: Timeline: quick RFC doc this week, 1-week spike next sprint. Volunteers: tom + irene for loader + platform hooks.

alice: I'll write RFC tonight with proto sketch for manifest and token-bucket defaults. Thanks all :thumbsup:
